mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen every week for the last three weeks (-35.3, -32.3, -31.3, -29.9). This monotonic recovery momentum reflects gradually loosening behavioral constraints and will persist, pushing the next-28-day mean above the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly mean reverses and declines for two or more consecutive weeks following t-0w, pulling the 28-day forward mean below the trailing 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped sharply from -8.4 to +7.7 in the latest week, a discrete break from its prior range, consistent with relaxed outdoor-gathering restrictions. Such policy easing typically precedes a parallel loosening of retail-and-recreation limits within two weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week increase exceeds 10 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -8.4 at t-1w to 7.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after a PARKS jump exceeding 10 points, or if PARKS gains reverse without retail follow-through, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both been improving together (TRANSIT: -36.6 to -30.4; WORKPLACES: -27.4 to -21.1), indicating a joint normalization of commuting and work-related travel. When both series trend upward simultaneously, combined mobility recovery spills into shopping and leisure trips, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to improve jointly, or if the joint rise does not outperform single-series predictions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sudden surge in PARKS mobility coincides with the seasonal onset of warmer spring weather in Madrid. As residents substitute outdoor park visits for indoor retail and recreation trips, RETAIL_REC growth will be dampened or reversed over the following two weeks even as overall mobility recovers.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS turned positive (7.7) while RETAIL_REC remains negative (-29.9)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues rising at the same or faster pace despite sustained high PARKS values, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been declining (10.9 to 8.1 over four weeks), indicating people are spending less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL falls below a threshold of 8.0, it signals sufficient behavioral loosening that out-of-home retail and recreation activity will rise within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8.0 percentage points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 10.9 to 8.1 over the last four weeks
regime_hint: any regime with declining residential time
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 8.0 but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, or declines instead, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near baseline (-0.7 at t-0w, up from -5.3 three weeks prior), suggesting no new essential-only restrictions are being imposed. In the absence of tightening, the gradual retail recovery trend continues uninterrupted over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -5.3 to -0.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline but RETAIL_REC declines week-over-week, the no-restriction-implies-growth linkage is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and decline in RESIDENTIAL together indicate a compound behavioral shift away from home-centric routines toward broader out-of-home activity. This three-way co-movement amplifies retail footfall growth beyond what any single series predicts over a two-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose while RESIDENTIAL fell across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth over two weeks is no greater than what TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone would predict, or if RETAIL_REC declines despite all three series moving favorably, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The single-week PARKS spike to 7.7 without confirming increases in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES suggests a transient weather-driven weekend effect rather than a durable policy or behavioral shift. Such unconfirmed spikes tend to mean-revert, and RETAIL_REC growth will stall or dip in the immediate following week as the anomaly fades.
candidate_trigger: PARKS single-week increase exceeds 15 points without TRANSIT or WORKPLACES confirming a comparable jump
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped 15.1 points while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES changed only modestly
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week immediately following an unconfirmed PARKS spike, the mean-reversion hypothesis is rejected.
